rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In conditional pairs, an explicit كان makes the intended relation clear; after fa, a nominative predicate is more usual because the answer resumes as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: الفاء فى جواب الجزاء استأنفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative after the conditional particle is also possible: the answer is jussive, and its noun is analogized to a predicate, although the analogy is not complete.
rows.anchor: كان النصب فيما هو جوابه لأنه يجزم كما يجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the verb is omitted, suppressing the accusative-governing verb is better; omitting a nominative-governing verb also requires omitting its predicate, and extra ellipsis weakens the parse.
rows.anchor: وإذا أضمرت فأن تضمر الناصب أحسن لأنك إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A following adjective or appositive tied to the previously mentioned person must be accusative; حق or كذب can instead introduce an independent condition with its own omitted كان or وقع.
rows.anchor: تستطيع أن لا تحمله على الأول فتقول إن كان فيه حق

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus reports Hudba ibn Khashram’s verse as an Arabic example of an إن clause whose verbal material is understood from context.
rows.anchor: يونس أن العرب تنشد هذا البيت لهدبة بن خشرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layla al-Akhyaliyya, Ibn Hammam al-Sululi, and al-Nabigha illustrate accusative adjectives or descriptions that remain tied to the person named earlier in the clause.
rows.anchor: لا تقربن الدهر آل مطرف

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus attributes to some Arabs إن لا صالح فطالح, understood as an omitted مررت clause: if I did not meet a righteous person, I met a wicked one.
rows.anchor: أن من العرب من يقول إن لا صالح فطالح على إن لا أكن مررت بصالح فبطالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh calls that analysis weak because it requires an extra omitted verb after إن لا; the fuller إن لا يكن صالحا فطالح requires less ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وهذا قبيح ضعيف لأنك تضمر بعد إن لا فعلا آخر فيه حذف غير الذى تضمر بعد إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن of condition does not directly govern a noun: any accusative or nominative after it depends on an omitted verb, while a genitive name belongs to a suppressed prepositional phrase such as مررت بزيد.
rows.anchor: ولا يرتفع إلا بفعل لأن إن من الحروف التى يبنى عليها الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In من لد شولا, شولا is accusative because it means a time; an omitted أن كانت supplies that temporal sense, though some allow genitive by broad usage.
rows.anchor: الشول لا يكون زمانا ولا مكانا فيجوز فيها الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ellipsis is limited to particles and constructions where Arabs use it; one cannot extend a deletion pattern to every particle or verb by analogy.
rows.anchor: يظهر بعده الفعل يحذف فيه الفعل ولكنك تضمر بعد ما أضمرت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the poem فإن جزعا وإن إجمال صبر, إن is a shortened إما meaning either, not conditional إن: the fa and lack of a conditional answer support the parse, as in 47:4.
rows.anchor: فليس قوله فإن جزعا كقوله إن حقا وإن كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping ما from إما is poetic only; al-Namr ibn Tawlab’s verse illustrates it, and reading the same form as conditional إن requires a separately omitted verb.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز طرح ما من إما إلا فى الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responses such as هلا خيرا or ألا خيرا use an omitted verb that would be spoken; a nominative is possible when a nominative-governing verb is understood.
rows.anchor: كأنك قلت : ألا تفعل خيرا من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أو فرقا خيرا من حب, the accusative answers a question about an action and implies أفرقك; a nominative would instead present فرق as a topic.
rows.anchor: وإنما حمله على الفعل لأنه سئل عن فعله فأجابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ولو, an apparent noun normally rests on an omitted كان or يكون, so ولو حمارا is preferred; a nominative is possible but remote because لو selects verbs.
rows.anchor: ولو قلت ولو حمار فجررت كان بمنزلته فى إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adjective after ولو must be accusative because it cannot stand in place of a noun; the source contrasts ولو باردا with the acceptable noun ائتنى بتمر.
rows.anchor: لم يحسن إلا النصب لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ادفع الشر ولو إصبعا means even if you push it a finger’s breadth or it were a finger; accusative follows the implied action, while raising is less natural.
rows.anchor: ولو إصبعا كأنه قال ولو دفعته إصبعا ولو كان إصبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After news of an arrival or dream, خير مقدم and خيرا can be accusative as an omitted verbal response; nominative makes an independent statement such as هذا خير مقدم.
rows.anchor: ولكنه قال هذا خير مقدم وهذا خير لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Formulae like مصاحب معان and مبرور مأجور are nominative with an understood أنت; راشدا مهديا is commonly accusative with اذهب, though raising is also possible.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم قالوا مصاحب معان ومبرور مأجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reply صادقا والله after a report means قاله صادقا; its accusative is licensed by the implied act of saying or reciting.
rows.anchor: أو أنشدك شعرا فتقول صادقا والله أى قاله صادقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In متعرضا لعنن لم يعنه, the omitted verb is recoverable from the visible situation: the person has approached an undertaking without being summoned to it.
rows.anchor: فتقول متعرضا لعنن لم يعنه أى دنا من هذا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In bargaining, بيع الملطى omits أبايعك; مواعيد عرقوب similarly omits واعدتني because the shared situation and prior history supply the verb.
rows.anchor: وذلك إن كنت فى حال مساومة وحال بيع فتدع أبايعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs use nominatives such as متعرض or صادق والله; Sibawayh also explains غضب الخيل على اللجم through an implied verb, with some speakers raising it instead.
rows.anchor: غضب الخيل على اللجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After someone mentions a person, أهل ذاك or أهله can mean you mentioned his family; accusative follows the semantic act, while nominative supplies هو.
rows.anchor: ومثله أن تسمع الرجل ذكر فتقول أهل ذاك وأهله أى ذكرت أهله لأنك فى ذكره

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil allows من and ما here to be indefinite common nouns like إنسان and شيء, with what follows functioning as an adjective.
rows.anchor: رحمه الله إن شئت جعلت من بمنزلة إنسان وجعلت ما بمنزلة شئ نكرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the alternate construction, من and ما serve as relative forms that require a following complement; the words are not intended to stand empty of either complement or description.
rows.anchor: لحشوهما ولوصفهما ولم يرد بهما خلوين شئ فلزمه الوصف كما لزمه الحشو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the following material is a relative complement, من and ما are definite, like الذي; the source applies this rule to the dependent clause after الذي.
rows.anchor: فكما أن الذي لا يكون إلا معرفة لا يكون ما ومن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In هذا من أعرف منطلق, أعرف is an adjective; in هذا من أعرف منطلقا it is a relative complement, while منطلق can also be a predicate as in هذا عبد الله منطلق.
rows.anchor: وتقول هذا من أعرف منطلق فتجعل أعرف صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا أيها is a means of reaching a noun with the definite article, and الرجل describes أيها; the phrase cannot stop at يا أيها alone.
rows.anchor: يصير وصفه عندهم كأنه به يتم الاسم لأنهم إنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In الجماء الغفير, الغفير is a required descriptive emphasis, illustrating how a noun can need its descriptor to complete the expression.
rows.anchor: فلزم الغفير كما لزم ما في قولك إنك ما وخيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh calls كفى بنا فضلا على من غيرنا the stronger construction, though weak without هو, and compares it to a reading of 6:154 with a relative complement.
rows.anchor: أجود وفيه ضعف إلا أن يكون فيه هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh gives two nominative analyses for هذا ما لدى عتيد, including an analysis with an understood شيء and another treating the larger expression as a predicate.
rows.anchor: على وجهين على شئ لدى عنيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction رب من supports taking من as indefinite because what follows رب is always indefinite; Amr ibn Qumai'a, Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt, and other poets provide examples.
rows.anchor: أن من نكرة قول عمرو بن قميئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هذا من منطلق is awkward when منطلق is a complement or adjective, but longer wording such as من خير منك works; al-Khalil heard Arabs say ما أنا بالذي قائل لك سوءا.
rows.anchor: فقلت من خير منك حسن

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reports hearing an Arab say ما أنا بالذي قائل لك سوءا and ما أنا بالذي قائل لك قبيحا, showing a descriptive complement after الذي.
rows.anchor: قائل لك سوءا وما أنا بالذي قائل لك قبيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doubled verb has two identical consonants at its end, as in رددت and وددت; this is the morphological class of the verse's مضارّ form.
rows.anchor: والتضعيف أن يكون آخر الفعل حرفان من موضع واحد وذلك نحو

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: When both final consonants are vowelled, Arabs agree on assimilation; al-Khalil says it is especially apt because repeating the same articulation is burdensome.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما كانا من موضع واحد ثقل عليهم

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: The Hijaz dialect keeps the doubled consonants separate when the verb ending is quiescent, moving the preceding consonant to avoid two sukūns together.
rows.anchor: فإن أهل الحجاز يضاعفون لأنهم

rows.speaker: بنو تميم
rows.claim: Banu Tamim assimilate the jussive as well as fully vowelled forms; Sibawayh says many other Arabs share this dialect pattern.
rows.anchor: وأما بنو تميم فيدغمون المجزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the consonant before the first of the doubled pair is quiescent, it takes that consonant’s vowel; a now-unneeded alif of connection is deleted.
rows.anchor: ألقيت حركة الأول منهما على الساكن الذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an alif before the doubled consonants and no alif of connection, the form remains unchanged; لا تضار is one of Sibawayh’s examples.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك ماد ولا تضار ولا تجار وكذلك ما كانت ألفه مقطوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A following kasra on ر can make a preceding open vowel incline toward kasra: the ر is like two kasra-bearing consonants, so Sibawayh analogizes its effect to ي.
rows.anchor: من الضرر ومن البعر ومن الكبر ومن الصغر ومن الفقر لما كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imala is blocked when an open vowel follows the alif or when an emphatic consonant resists it, as in المحاذر and حاضر.
rows.anchor: وتقول المحاذر فتميل الذال ولا تقوى على إمالة الألف لأن بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ابن مذعور, the speaker approaches kasra after ر but does not incline the و, since it does not resemble ي and tilting it would also tilt what precedes.
rows.anchor: وتقول هذا ابن مذعور كأنك تروم الكسرة لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A following separate word with ر and kasra can cause imala across the word boundary, as in خبط رياح and قفا رياح.
rows.anchor: رأيت خبط رياح فتميل طاء خبط للراء المنفصلة المكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other speakers leave forms uninclined when the conditioning kasra is too far away across a word boundary, as in مال قاسم, خبط رياح, and قفا رياح.
rows.anchor: وأما من قال مررت بمال قاسم فلم ينصب لأنها منفصلة قال رأيت خبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers incline before ر in من عمرو but not من الشرق because the latter ر is followed by an emphatic consonant; this also blocks the pattern in مارق.
rows.anchor: الشرق لأن بعد الراء حرفا مستعليا فلا يكون ذا كما لم يكن هذا مارق
